key_insight: Lower observation frequency increased prediction error, but frequency-specific RNNs retained a 24–30% advantage over the better kinematic baseline on straight motion and turns at every tested frequency.
engineering_relevance: For sparse V2X observations, a 10 Hz RNN with linear interpolation nearly matched frequency-specific training down to 2 Hz, but was 11.5% less accurate at 1 Hz.
method: Downsampled 5 s focal-agent histories from 10 Hz to 5, 2, and 1 Hz to predict 6 s futures.
Compared frequency-specific LSTM RNNs with constant-velocity and constant-acceleration models.
Tested a 10 Hz RNN on linearly interpolated sparse histories, without maps or neighboring agents.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 24,984 Argoverse 2 test scenarios, ten training seeds per main RNN, predefined hypotheses and thresholds, and bootstrap confidence intervals over scenarios and seeds.
watch_item: The RNN advantage did not extend to pedestrians, for whom constant velocity was more accurate; results also exclude map and neighboring-agent context.
paper_title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
